questions.question:
Consider the following two reactions A and B.

Numerical value of [molar mass of $x+$ molar mass of $y$] is $\_\_\_\_$.
questions.solution:
Reaction A: Phenol reacts with metallic sodium to produce sodium phenoxide and hydrogen gas.
C₆H₅OH + Na → C₆H₅ONa + ½H₂.
The gas evolved is x = H₂ with molar mass 2 g/mol.
Reaction B: Benzoic acid reacts with sodium bicarbonate to produce sodium benzoate, water, and carbon dioxide.
C₆H₅COOH + NaHCO₃ → C₆H₅COONa + H₂O + CO₂.
The gas evolved is y = CO₂ with molar mass 44 g/mol.
Therefore, molar mass of x + molar mass of y = 2 + 44 = 46.

questions.q: Grignard reagent $\mathrm{RMgBr}(\mathrm{P})$ reacts with water and forms a gas (Q). One gram of Q occupies $1.4 \mathrm{dm}^{3}$ at STP. (P) on reaction with dry ice in dry ether followed by $\mathrm{H}_{3} \mathrm{O}^{+}$forms a compound (Z). 0.1 mole of (Z) will weigh $\_\_\_\_$ g. (Nearest integer)
questions.question: Grignard reagent $\mathrm{RMgBr}(\mathrm{P})$ reacts with water and forms a gas (Q). One gram of Q occupies $1.4 \mathrm{dm}^{3}$ at STP. (P) on reaction with dry ice in dry ether followed by $\mathrm{H}_{3} \mathrm{O}^{+}$forms a compound (Z). 0.1 mole of (Z) will weigh $\_\_\_\_$ g. (Nearest integer)
questions.solution:
Grignard reagent RMgBr reacts with water to produce gas Q.
One gram of Q occupies 1.4 L at STP.
Moles of Q = 1.4/22.4 = 0.0625 mol, so molar mass = 1/0.0625 = 16 g/mol, identifying Q as CH₄.
Thus P = CH₃MgBr.
When P reacts with dry ice: $\text{CH}_3\text{MgBr} + \text{CO}_2 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COOMgBr}$.
Upon treatment with H₃O⁺, this gives Z = CH₃COOH (acetic acid).
Molar mass of Z = 60 g/mol.
Mass of 0.1 mol = 0.1 × 60 = 6 g.

questions.q:
Complete the following reaction sequence and give the name of major product 'P'.
$CH_3-CH_2-C\equiv N \xrightarrow[\text{(ii) } H_3O^+]{\text{(i) } OH^-/H_2O/\Delta} \xrightarrow[\text{(iv) } H_2O]{\text{(iii) } Cl_2/\text{Red P}} P \text{ (Major product)}$
questions.question:
Complete the following reaction sequence and give the name of major product 'P'.
$CH_3-CH_2-C\equiv N \xrightarrow[\text{(ii) } H_3O^+]{\text{(i) } OH^-/H_2O/\Delta} \xrightarrow[\text{(iv) } H_2O]{\text{(iii) } Cl_2/\text{Red P}} P \text{ (Major product)}$
questions.solution:
Step 1: Hydrolysis of the nitrile.
Propanenitrile on basic hydrolysis followed by acidic workup gives propanoic acid:
$CH_3-CH_2-C \equiv N \xrightarrow[(ii)\ H_3O^+]{(i)\ OH^-/H_2O/\Delta} CH_3-CH_2-COOH$

Step 2: Hell$-$Volhard$-$Zelinsky (HVZ) reaction.
Propanoic acid has an $sp^3$ $\alpha$-carbon bearing two $\alpha$-hydrogens. In the HVZ reaction, $Cl_2$ in the presence of red phosphorus selectively replaces one $\alpha$-hydrogen by chlorine, giving the $\alpha$-chloro acid after aqueous workup:
$CH_3-CH_2-COOH \xrightarrow[(iv)\ H_2O]{(iii)\ Cl_2/\text{Red P}} CH_3-CH(Cl)-COOH$

Hence, the major product $P$ is $2$-chloropropanoic acid, which corresponds to option $(1)$.

Step 2: Hell$-$Volhard$-$Zelinsky (HVZ) reaction.
Propanoic acid has an $sp^3$ $\alpha$-carbon bearing two $\alpha$-hydrogens. In the HVZ reaction, $Cl_2$ in the presence of red phosphorus selectively replaces one $\alpha$-hydrogen by chlorine, giving the $\alpha$-chloro acid after aqueous workup:
$CH_3-CH_2-COOH \xrightarrow[(iv)\ H_2O]{(iii)\ Cl_2/\text{Red P}} CH_3-CH(Cl)-COOH$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Methane can be prepared by decarboxylation of sodium ethanoate, Kolbe's electrolysis of sodium acetate and reaction of $\text{CH}_3\text{MgBr}$ with water.

Statement II: Methane cannot be prepared from unsaturated hydrocarbons and by Wurtz reaction.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
questions.question:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Methane can be prepared by decarboxylation of sodium ethanoate, Kolbe's electrolysis of sodium acetate and reaction of $\text{CH}_3\text{MgBr}$ with water.

Statement II: Methane cannot be prepared from unsaturated hydrocarbons and by Wurtz reaction.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.solution:
Statement I is false because Kolbe's electrolysis of sodium acetate produces ethane, not methane. The reaction is: $2\text{CH}_3\text{COONa} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{Electrolysis}} \text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_3 + 2\text{CO}_2 + \text{H}_2 + 2\text{NaOH}$. Decarboxylation of sodium ethanoate and the reaction of $\text{CH}_3\text{MgBr}$ with water do produce methane.

Statement II is true because the simplest unsaturated hydrocarbon is ethene ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$), which upon hydrogenation yields ethane, meaning methane cannot be prepared from unsaturated hydrocarbons. Additionally, the Wurtz reaction involves the coupling of two alkyl halide molecules to form an alkane with at least two carbon atoms ($2\text{RX} + 2\text{Na} \rightarrow \text{R}-\text{R} + 2\text{NaX}$), so methane cannot be prepared by this method.

Therefore, Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

Answer: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.explanation:
Statement I is false because Kolbe's electrolysis of sodium acetate produces ethane, not methane. The reaction is: $2\text{CH}_3\text{COONa} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{Electrolysis}} \text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_3 + 2\text{CO}_2 + \text{H}_2 + 2\text{NaOH}$. Decarboxylation of sodium ethanoate and the reaction of $\text{CH}_3\text{MgBr}$ with water do produce methane.

Statement II is true because the simplest unsaturated hydrocarbon is ethene ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$), which upon hydrogenation yields ethane, meaning methane cannot be prepared from unsaturated hydrocarbons. Additionally, the Wurtz reaction involves the coupling of two alkyl halide molecules to form an alkane with at least two carbon atoms ($2\text{RX} + 2\text{Na} \rightarrow \text{R}-\text{R} + 2\text{NaX}$), so methane cannot be prepared by this method.

Therefore, Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

Answer: Statement I is false but Statement II is true

questions.q: Number of alkanes obtained on electrolysis of a mixture of ${CH}_{3}COONa$ and ${C}_{2}{H}_{5}COONa$ is_____.
questions.question: Number of alkanes obtained on electrolysis of a mixture of ${CH}_{3}COONa$ and ${C}_{2}{H}_{5}COONa$ is_____.
questions.solution:
An aqueous solution of sodium or potassium salt of carboxylic acid is electrolysed in this reaction, resulting in the dissociation of the salt into a carboxylate ion and sodium or potassium ions. 

The total number of different alkanes are formed when the following mixture is subjected to electrolysis:

${CH}_{3}COONa\left(aq\right)and{C}_{2}{H}_{5}COONa\left(aq\right)$ 

In this ethane, butane and propane are formed.

${CH}_{3}COONa \to \overset{∙}{C}{H}_{3}$

${C}_{2}{H}_{5}COONa \to \overset{∙}{C}2{H}_{5}$

$2\overset{∙}{C}2{H}_{5} \to {CH}_{3} - {CH}_{2} - {CH}_{2} - {CH}_{3}$

$2C\overset{∙}{H}3 \to {CH}_{3} - {CH}_{3}$

$\overset{∙}{C}{H}_{3} + \overset{∙}{C}2{H}_{5} \to {CH}_{3} - {CH}_{2} - {CH}_{3}$

So, the total number of alkanes formed here will be $3$

questions.solution:
The reaction sequence proceeds as follows:

The reagent $\text{NaBH}_4$ is a mild reducing agent that selectively reduces the aldehyde group ($-\text{CHO}$) to a primary alcohol ($-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$). The lactam (cyclic amide) ring remains unaffected.
